dct_description_sm: The aim of the North Greenland Eemian Ice Drilling (NEEM) project is to retrieve an ice core which reaches through the previous interglacial period, the Eemian, and beyond.  The Eemian lasted from about 130,000 to 115,000 years ago.  Part of that interglacial is thought to have been warmer than present by as much as 5C.  The scientific objective of NEEM is to gain, through the most detailed ice core analysis possible, a better understanding of the dynamics of climate, particularly during warmer conditions than present.  To that end, many different types of measurements will be used.  Pollen samples will be extracted at regular intervals along the ice core.  The resolution will be higher during the transition periods and throughout the Eemian. The pollen assemblages obtained from the NEEM ice core should reflect changes in the vegetation cover over time.  It is also expected that pollen concentrations will be higher than at present for parts of the Eemian period and lower during colder periods.
dct_title_s: Pollen analysis of the NEEM ice core, northern Greenland
